skill.name: threejs-lighting
skill.description: Light types and physical units, shadow maps, HDR environment lighting, light probes, and lighting performance, on WebGL or with WebGPU and TSL. Use when adding or tuning lights, fixing shadow acne, setting up image-based lighting, or dimming an environment map.
skill.summary: Set up and tune lights, shadows, and HDR environments in Three.js for WebGL or WebGPU.
skill.author: cloudai-x

content.user_title: Light Three.js Scenes and Tune Shadows
content.value_statement: Renderer differences and light intensity units can make Three.js scenes hard to light consistently. Use renderer-specific examples to choose lights, tune shadows, and set up HDR environment lighting.
actual_capabilities: Compare light types by intensity units, falloff, and shadow support.
Configure shadow casting and receiving, then tune map resolution, camera bounds, and bias.
Set up HDR or cube environment lighting and control lighting intensity separately from background brightness.
Generate ambient light probes from cube captures or bake a grid for position-dependent lighting.
Adapt lighting setups to WebGPU, including area light texture registration and per-material light selection with TSL.
Reduce shadow rendering work by limiting shadow casters or updating static shadow maps only when needed.
limitations: Examples target Three.js r186, so check API availability when using another revision.
The skill provides reference examples, not an automated visual test or GPU benchmark.
HDR and cube map examples require image assets supplied by your project.
Some examples assume an existing scene, camera, and renderer.

use_cases.title: Light a product viewer
use_cases.description: Set up HDR reflections for a product and adjust its lighting without changing the background brightness.

use_cases.title: Fix outdoor shadow artifacts
use_cases.description: Tune the directional shadow camera and bias, or evaluate cascaded shadows for a larger scene.

use_cases.title: Adapt a scene to WebGPU
use_cases.description: Identify renderer-specific lighting setup changes and assign selected lights to a node material.

prompt_templates.title: Add a light and shadow
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: A box sits above a floor in a WebGL scene.
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me how to add a directional light so the box casts a shadow on the floor. List the settings for the renderer, light, and meshes.

prompt_templates.title: Separate HDR lighting from the background
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: A product viewer uses an HDR environment.
prompt_templates.prompt: Show how to load my HDR image in Three.js r186. Reduce its lighting intensity without changing the background brightness.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose directional shadow artifacts
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: A WebGL scene shows jagged shadows and dark surface speckles.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my directional shadow settings. Explain how to adjust camera bounds, map resolution, and bias, and suggest an order for testing the changes.

prompt_templates.title: Plan lighting for many WebGPU point lights
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: A WebGPU scene has many unshadowed point lights.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare clustered and dynamic lighting for my Three.js r186 scene. Explain the shadow constraints and how TSL can restrict a node material to selected lights.

output_examples.input: My box casts no shadow in WebGL. What should I check?
output: Enable shadow maps on the renderer.
Enable shadow casting on the directional light and the box.
Enable shadow receiving on the floor and check that both meshes fit within the light's shadow camera.

output_examples.input: How can I make the HDR reflections dimmer without darkening the visible sky?
output: Lower the scene environment intensity and leave the background intensity unchanged.
For a material with its own environment map, adjust that material's environment map intensity instead.

best_practices: State your Three.js revision and renderer before adapting an example.
Use a camera helper to verify directional shadow bounds before increasing map resolution.
Disable shadow casting on lights that do not need it, especially point lights that require six shadow passes.
anti_patterns: Do not rely on removed legacy lighting flags to restore brightness. Retune point and spot lights for their distance and candela values.
Do not use light layers to select individual meshes. The renderer tests light layers against the camera.
Do not manually prefilter an equirectangular HDR texture when assigning it directly as the scene environment. The renderer handles prefiltering.

faq.question: Which Three.js version and renderers does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It targets r186 and uses WebGLRenderer for most examples. A separate section covers WebGPURenderer and TSL.

faq.question: Can a rectangular area light cast shadows?
faq.answer: No. It provides soft illumination for standard and physical materials but does not cast shadows.

faq.question: Why is my point light dim at a distance?
faq.answer: Point light intensity uses candela and falls off with the square of distance by default. Tune intensity for the scale of your scene.

faq.question: Should I increase shadow map resolution to fix shadow acne?
faq.answer: Start with small bias or normal bias adjustments. Tight shadow camera bounds and higher resolution help with jagged edges.

faq.question: When should I use a light probe instead of an environment map?
faq.answer: Use a light probe for baked ambient illumination. Use an environment map for image-based lighting that also provides reflections.

faq.question: Can I change the HDR lighting without changing the background?
faq.answer: Yes. The scene has separate intensity and rotation settings for environment lighting and the visible background.
